newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestry jitters keep Helsinki from testing highs.
newsitem.headline: Forestry jitters keep Helsinki from testing highs.

text.p: Shares remained close to year-highs but ended lively Wednesday session a shade lower as forestries slipped ahead of UPM's and Metsa-Serla's eight-month reports, brokers said.
"It depends on the UPM data whether forestries continue to slide," one broker said. Shares in Europe's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene lost 1.20 markka at 92.90 in cautious trade.

Merita advanced to 14.00 markka -- its highest since July 12, 1995 -- up 0.50 in brisk demand after buy recommendations. Its competitor Okobank closed fair trade at 47.50 markka -- up 0.70 -- where it last traded on January 18, 1995.
The HEX set its calendar year-high 2,226.6 on October 8.

Pharmaceuticals wholesaler Tamro gained 0.50 markka to 32.50 ahead of eight-month data due on Thursday with volume boosted by a 40 million markka in-house deal by Protos Stockbrokers. Protos declined comment on the deal, and Tamro said it did not know who traded the stock.
Engineering groups Rauma and Tampella also gained slightly in moderate trade ahead of January-August reports.
Cargo shipping firm Finnlines rose 2.50 markka to 108.00, its highest close since November 1995, as analysts said its chance to up its BTL stake may justify a yet higher valuation.
Food and chemicals group Raisio returned to sharp gains, ending up 16.00 markka at 279.00 after solid dealings ahead of the group's update on its cholesterol-reducing Benecol margarine on October 24.
